source.title: Enhanced Sample Selection with Confidence Tracking: Identifying Correctly Labeled Yet Hard-to-Learn Samples in Noisy Data
source.authors: Wei-Ran Pan; Wei Wei; Fei-Da Zhu; Yong Deng

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study measures gradient alignment during training on noisy labels, a different measure bearing on whether correct labels are learned before noisy labels are memorized.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own gradient-alignment measurements on CIFAR-10N-Worst and states that the results align with early learning. Its benchmark accuracy and sample-selection results do not measure the claim versions. Cited memorization results are not counted as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study uses early learning to design a noisy-label selector. Its gradient-alignment and prediction-confidence trajectories measure optimization direction and confidence changes, not whether correct patterns are fitted before noisy labels are memorized. Benchmark accuracy and selection performance do not establish any claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately describes the authors' interpretation of their alignment analysis as evidence consistent with early learning, but understates the paper's main conclusion: Confidence Tracking improves identification of hard correctly labeled samples and enhances existing noisy-label learning methods. The authors do not directly demonstrate the fitting sequence required by V6.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures gradient alignment on human-annotated noisy CIFAR-10N-Worst samples, rather than fitting completely random labels and measuring training/test error as in the original claim sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported alignment behavior differs between training without sample selection and training with GMM+CT sample selection.

fits_no_version.finding: Without sample selection, ground-truth gradient alignment is highest early; annotated-label alignment later overtakes it for mislabeled samples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On sampled CIFAR-10N-Worst groups, SGD updates initially favor ground-truth confidence growth and later favor noisy annotations.

fits_no_version.finding: With GMM+CT, noisy-label alignment is not highest during most of training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing suspected mislabeled samples can keep optimization from becoming dominated by their annotated labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 shows different early confidence trajectories for hard correctly labeled dogs and cats mislabeled as dogs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early prediction-confidence trends can distinguish some correct and incorrect annotations even when their losses overlap.

record.problems: The claim-relevant evidence is a gradient-alignment proxy rather than direct measurements of fitting order or training error. The figures provide no numeric values in the text. The empirical analysis uses CIFAR-10N-Worst and sampled examples; no uncertainty estimates are stated for these measurements.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Benchmark test accuracies and sample-selection precision/recall are outside the claim versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on completely random labels with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and chance test performance.
Random-label versus true-label fitting time and convergence across corruption fractions; CT overhead is a different comparison.
Zero-error fitting of shuffled, independently permuted, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit alongside steadily degrading test performance across a clean-to-fully-random label sweep.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing it harms true-label generalization.
Direct measurements establishing that shared real-data patterns are fitted before noisy or random labels are memorized.

record.verdict_notes: The authors explicitly connect their proxies to early learning, but that interpretation does not make them direct measurements of fitting or memorization. Neither missing numerical alignment values nor sample-selection effects establish partial or absent V6 behavior.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks fit completely random labels to near-zero training error with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and whether test error is at chance.
Training-time cost relative to true labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across a sweep from clean to fully random labels.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent random-label fitting or whether their removal harms true-label generalization.
The measurements are gradient-alignment proxies on CIFAR-10N-Worst, not direct measurements of fitting patterns shared by real data before memorizing noisy labels over training.

rows.subject: PreActResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measured gradient alignment for correctly labeled cat images during training.
rows.measure: Gradient alignment Ac for ground-truth and annotated labels
rows.note: The text says Ay is highest on correctly labeled samples in the early training stage; only after a period does Aŷ exceed Ay. The plotted values are not stated numerically.
rows.check: Gradient alignment does not measure fitting order. For correctly labeled cat samples, ground-truth and annotated labels coincide, so their alignments cannot cross; the record incorrectly applies the later crossover statement to this group.

rows.subject: PreActResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measured gradient alignment for mislabeled cat images during training.
rows.measure: Gradient alignment Ac for ground-truth and annotated labels
rows.note: The text says Ay is highest on mislabeled samples in the early training stage; only after a period does Aŷ exceed Ay. The plotted values are not stated numerically.
rows.check: Early ground-truth alignment followed by stronger annotated-label alignment measures a change in optimization direction, without establishing when either label is fitted or memorized.

rows.subject: PreActResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measured gradient alignment for correctly labeled truck images during training.
rows.measure: Gradient alignment Ac for ground-truth and annotated labels
rows.note: The text gives the early-versus-later alignment result for correctly labeled samples generally; plotted values for this sample are not stated numerically.
rows.check: Gradient alignment does not measure fitting order. Ground-truth and annotated labels coincide for correctly labeled truck samples; the record's general crossover interpretation cannot apply to them.

rows.subject: PreActResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measured gradient alignment for mislabeled truck images during training.
rows.measure: Gradient alignment Ac for ground-truth and annotated labels
rows.note: The text gives the early-versus-later alignment result for mislabeled samples generally; plotted values for this sample are not stated numerically.
rows.check: The alignment trajectories do not establish correct-label fitting followed by incorrect-label memorization.

rows.subject: PreActResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measured gradient alignment for correctly labeled samples during training with GMM+CT sample selection.
rows.measure: Gradient alignment Ac for ground-truth and annotated labels
rows.note: Figure 5 shows two correctly labeled sample types; the text describes the result for noisy-label alignment under GMM+CT but gives no numeric values.
rows.check: This is a diagnostic of training with the proposed sample-selection method, rather than a claim-result row. Correctly labeled samples also have identical ground-truth and annotated labels.

rows.subject: PreActResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measured gradient alignment for mislabeled samples during training with GMM+CT sample selection.
rows.measure: Gradient alignment Ac for ground-truth and annotated labels
rows.note: The authors state that after sample selection, alignment with noisy labels is not highest during most of training; plotted values are not stated numerically.
rows.check: This method diagnostic concerns suppression of noisy-label gradient alignment after sample selection, not measured fitting order. It does not justify a limits_scope verdict on V6.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The authors report ground-truth-label alignment is highest early for both correctly labeled and mislabeled samples, with annotated-label alignment larger only after a period (R1–R4); this is indirect evidence for early learning, not a direct fit measure.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported alignment result is conditional on sample selection: alignment with noisy labels is not highest during most of training (R5–R6).
